# 1. What the Research Found

**MONITORING. Re-check window: the trial's next reporting milestone and DP World's stated strategic-review outcome on permanently electrifying its route.**

FACT: "Called Project JOLT – standing for Joint Operator Logistics Trial – the programme is led by The Centre for Sustainable Road Freight (SRF) and involves partners including John Lewis Partnership, Volvo Trucks UK, and Flexible Power Systems, a software company specialising in fleet management optimisation software for electric vehicles." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "SRF was founded to help industry and government minimise carbon emissions from the road freight sector and is a collaboration between Cambridge University, Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh, the University of Westminster, and industry and government partners." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "The objective is to develop the knowledge and models needed to de-risk electric freight operations and inform investment decisions." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "It is driven by the Centre for Sustainable Road Freight and is made up of 15 fleet operators, four manufacturers, a charge point operator and three enablers." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "Evyve, the charge point operator, is providing high powered charging infrastructure and energy solutions for the initiative and subsequent roll outs." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "HGVs also account for 20% of CO 2 emissions from domestic transport." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "98% of our food and agricultural products are carried by road, mostly on HGVs." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "Freight is hugely important; it contributed £13.6 billion to the economy in 2022*." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "DP World has successfully trialled three electric vehicles under the Project Jolt initiative, which it joined three months ago. The three electric trucks were the Scania G230E truck and the Mercedes e-Actros 300, which was upgraded to the e-Actros 600 in the final 3 weeks." *Source: "DP World hails success of Project Jolt electric truck trial," Motor Transport, 12 August 2025. https://motortransport.co.uk/freightcarbonzero/dp-world-hails-success-of-project-jolt-electric-truck-trial/26783.article

FACT: "The company said that, although the cost of the electric truck is still high, the likely cost of electricity will create a favourable total cost of ownership compared to diesel and then of course there are the huge environmental gains." *Source: Motor Transport, 12 August 2025. https://motortransport.co.uk/freightcarbonzero/dp-world-hails-success-of-project-jolt-electric-truck-trial/26783.article

FACT: "Following the trial, DP World and its customer have carried out a strategic review on the commercial opportunity to permanently electrify this route." *Source: Motor Transport, 12 August 2025. https://motortransport.co.uk/freightcarbonzero/dp-world-hails-success-of-project-jolt-electric-truck-trial/26783.article

# 2. Why This Finding Matters Operationally and Commercially

FACT: "The trial will pool operations and technical data from a fleet of rigid and articulated eHGVs being used across a wide range of 3PL, retailer and manufacturer use cases." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

*Operational implication:* because the trial pools data across 3PL, retailer and manufacturer use cases, a workspace operating UK road-freight subcontracts with any of these profiles could, in principle, be operating alongside a participating fleet already generating comparable operational data -- relevant context when a client asks whether eHGV total-cost-of-ownership data exists for their own use case.

FACT: "The trial is open to all HGV operators becoming involved by accessing a shared vehicle fleet supplied by OEMs or sharing data from their own vehicles." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

*Operational implication:* the trial's own stated openness to any HGV operator (via a shared OEM-supplied fleet or by sharing data from an operator's own vehicles) means the workspace's own road-freight subcontractors are, in principle, eligible to participate if not already doing so -- worth raising directly with a UK road subcontractor evaluating eHGV adoption.

FACT: "Specialists at Cambridge University and Heriot-Watt University will analyse and model data including vehicle and charger performance, operational efficiency, and costs across as many industry uses as possible." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "High resolution operational data will be collected during each trial period and then analysed, anonymised, and shared with all partners as part of a managed collective learning process." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

FACT: "All shared data will be subject to the provisions of a Data Confidentiality Agreement which will be agreed between all partners before the work starts." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

# 3. What the Finding Changes for Strategy, Claims, or Decisions

**1. TCO signal for road subcontractor electrification conversations, sourced to a live commercial trial rather than a lab estimate.**

*Analytical inference:* DP World's own stated finding, that electricity cost creates a favourable total cost of ownership relative to diesel despite the electric truck's higher purchase cost, is a real-world commercial-operator statement, not a modelled projection; it strengthens the workspace's position when advising a client or road subcontractor evaluating eHGV adoption.

**2. A named-carrier permanent-electrification decision is pending, not yet made.**

FACT: "Following the trial, DP World and its customer have carried out a strategic review on the commercial opportunity to permanently electrify this route." *Source: Motor Transport, 12 August 2025. https://motortransport.co.uk/freightcarbonzero/dp-world-hails-success-of-project-jolt-electric-truck-trial/26783.article

*Operational implication:* DP World and its customer have only carried out a strategic review on permanently electrifying the trialled route; the workspace should not represent this route as already permanently electrified, and should monitor for the review's outcome (Section 5).

**3. Battery residual value remains an open research question, relevant to any road-fleet financing conversation.**

FACT: "Our research on battery performance is crucial to the ultimate findings on electrification and will help determine the residual value of electric trucks." *Source: Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering. https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial

*Analytical inference:* because the trial's own director frames battery residual value as still to be determined by this research, the workspace should treat eHGV residual-value assumptions in any client financing or leasing conversation as unresolved, not established.

# 4. Client Conversation Talking Points and Public Position

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- "Project JOLT, a live UK research trial led by the Centre for Sustainable Road Freight (Cambridge and Heriot-Watt universities) with partners including John Lewis Partnership, Volvo Trucks UK, and DP World, is generating real-world operational data on electric HGVs across 3PL, retailer, and manufacturer use cases."
- "HGVs account for 20% of UK domestic transport CO2 emissions, and 98% of UK food and agricultural products move by road, mostly on HGVs -- context UNCTAD-scale figures the Cambridge trial page itself cites for why this research matters."
- "DP World's own trial experience found that, despite a higher electric-truck purchase price, expected electricity costs create a favourable total cost of ownership versus diesel."

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

- Do not state that DP World's trialled route is now permanently electrified; only a strategic review of the opportunity has been carried out, per the trial's own reporting.
- Do not cite a specific cost-per-kilometre or total-cost-of-ownership figure for eHGVs generally; these are not publicly available from the captured pool, which reports only DP World's own qualitative favourable-TCO statement for its own trial.
- *Legal Confirmation Required:* specific regulatory deadlines and penalty provisions for UK or EU HGV CO2 standards are not grounded in the captured source content and require separate legal/regulatory research.

# 5. What the Finding Does Not Resolve

GAP: Specific regulatory deadlines and penalty provisions for UK or EU HGV CO2 standards are not grounded in the captured source content.

GAP: Do not cite specific cost-per-kilometre or total-cost-of-ownership figures for eHGVs generally; these are not publicly available from the captured pool.

GAP: While DP World states that the likely cost of electricity will create a favourable TCO compared to diesel, the captured pool does not provide the underlying quantitative TCO calculation or timeframe.

FACT: "DP World hails success of Project Jolt electric truck trial By Carol Millett 12 August 2025" *Source: Motor Transport. https://motortransport.co.uk/freightcarbonzero/dp-world-hails-success-of-project-jolt-electric-truck-trial/26783.article

*Operational implication:* the workspace's next monitoring pass should check for the outcome of DP World's strategic review on permanent electrification of the trialled route, and for any published Project JOLT interim or final research findings beyond this initial trial-period reporting.

- 12 Aug 2025: Motor Transport reported DP World's successful trial of three electric vehicles (Scania G230E, Mercedes e-Actros 300 upgraded to e-Actros 600) under Project JOLT, joined approximately three months earlier.

# 6. Sources

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Electric HGV trial, University of Cambridge Department of Engineering | Academic research programme page | https://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/electric-hgv-trial |
| 2 | "DP World hails success of Project Jolt electric truck trial," Motor Transport (Carol Millett, 12 August 2025) | Trade press | https://motortransport.co.uk/freightcarbonzero/dp-world-hails-success-of-project-jolt-electric-truck-trial/26783.article |
| 3 | Project JOLT homepage | Programme self-publication | https://jolt.eco/ |

*Note:* one captured block grounds no claim in this brief: the Commercial Motor article on the same

content.

entries.body:
# 1. Operational Cost Baseline for the Region

This profile synthesises current intelligence on the operational and infrastructure-investment environment for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in Brazil. It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is ocean, with road and air as secondary/tertiary, operating across high-value and time-sensitive cargo verticals, with Brazilian gateways serving primarily South American and transatlantic trade lanes.

The captured pool for this item is dominated by Brazilian government-portal navigation structure (the ANTT road-transport regulator, the ANP oil and gas regulator, ANEEL the electricity regulator, the Diario Oficial federal register, and the Senate) rather than article or dataset content; the one substantive capture is an ANTT news article on national transport-infrastructure investment, reproduced here in its own Portuguese with labelled English analysis (Section 6).

FACT: "Na FIESP, ANTT apresenta carteira de R$ 300 bilhões e reforça segurança para investimentos em infraestrutura no Brasil" *Source: ANTT (Agencia Nacional de Transportes Terrestres) news article, published 15/04/2026. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

FACT: "Hoje, o país conta com mais de 18 mil quilômetros de rodovias concedidas, com previsão de R$ 306 bilhões em investimentos (CAPEX) e R$ 219 bilhões destinados à operação e manutenção (OPEX)." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

*Per the workspace's reading:* this states a national CAPEX/OPEX envelope for Brazil's concessioned road network, not a per-shipment or per-lane operational cost the workspace can quote directly; it is the closest cost-scale signal the captured pool provides for Brazilian road infrastructure.

FACT: "No setor ferroviário, são 15 mil quilômetros operacionais, além de novos projetos estruturantes e ampliações em curso." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

FACT: "Atualmente, o setor ferroviário soma mais de R$ 227 bilhões em novos aportes, com milhares de quilômetros autorizados e dezenas de contratos vigentes." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

**Industrial electricity and fuel pricing.**

*No content for this section as of the export date: current industrial electricity tariff rates or fuel (diesel/bunker) pump prices for Brazil are not available from the captured source blocks. The ANEEL (electricity regulator) and ANP (oil and gas regulator) captures both returned only site-navigation structure, not tariff or price data; the ANEEL capture additionally carries a character-encoding defect (mojibake) in the small amount of body text it does contain, which is not reproduced here as a verbatim quote because it cannot be confirmed to be readable, undistorted source text.*

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

FACT: "No setor ferroviário, a agenda inclui novos leilões, renovações contratuais e projetos estratégicos, como a Ferrogrão e a EF-118, além da ampliação da malha existente." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

*Analytical inference:* the explicit naming of Ferrogrão and EF-118 as strategic rail projects alongside new auctions and contract renewals signals that rail-freight capacity expansion is an active national policy priority in Brazil, relevant to a workspace evaluating rail as a modal option for Brazilian inland corridors; the captured pool does not give a specific completion date, route capacity, or tariff for either named project (Section 5).

*No content for this section as of the export date: specific feasibility data for EV or alternative-fuel road-fleet adoption, warehouse retrofit costs, or port-side decarbonisation infrastructure in Brazil is not available from the captured source blocks.*

# 3. Cost Comparison Against Alternatives

*No content for this section as of the export date: specific numerical breakeven or payback data comparing operational choices (rail vs road, owned vs leased fleet, or any other alternative) in the Brazilian context are not available from the sourced blocks. This section is replaced by this honest note rather than filled with invented figures.*

# 4. Cross-Regional Strategic Implications

*No content for this section as of the export date: Cross-Regional Strategic Implications is a MATRIX-then-transitive comparison requiring the same cost or feasibility dimension sourced across at least two of the workspace's active regions. This record's stored pool covers only Brazil; no other regional_data item's sourced figures were supplied for this authoring pass, so no cross-regional comparison can be proven from this single stored pool. This omission will resolve once a second active region reaches sourced coverage on the same cost/feasibility dimensions.*

# 5. Competitive Positioning in the Region

*No content for this section as of the export date: named-competitor sustainability positioning or certification data for freight operators in Brazil is not available from the captured source blocks, which consist of Brazilian government-portal navigation structure and one national-infrastructure news article rather than any operator's own published material.*

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- *Per the workspace's reading:* Brazil's federal road-transport regulator (ANTT) has publicly presented a national investment pipeline of over BRL 300 billion (BRL 306 billion in planned road CAPEX plus BRL 219 billion in OPEX for the concessioned highway network alone), signalling sustained multi-year investment in the country's road and rail freight infrastructure.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* named strategic rail projects (Ferrogrão, EF-118) are part of the government's active 2026 agenda, relevant context for a client asking about future Brazilian rail-freight modal options, though the captured pool gives no completion timeline for either.

**What the workspace should not claim without verification:**

- Do not present the BRL 300+ billion investment figures as current operating costs or freight rates; they are national infrastructure CAPEX/OPEX and auction totals, not per-shipment or per-lane costs.
- Do not claim a specific Brazilian industrial electricity tariff or fuel price; the captured pool does not carry this data (Section 1).

**Questions the workspace can pose to clients:**

- "For Brazilian inland corridors, is your routing currently entirely road-based, or would a rail option become relevant once the Ferrogrão or EF-118 projects the government has flagged reach operational status?"

*Analytical inference:* these talking points draw only on the FACT and GAP claims already established in Sections 1 and 2 above; no new fact is introduced in this section.

# 7. Pending Changes That Shift the Calculus

### MONITORING

FACT: "Entre 2023 e 2025, foram realizados 19 leilões rodoviários, totalizando mais de 7 mil quilômetros concedidos e cerca de R$ 230 bilhões em investimentos." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

FACT: "Para 2026, estão previstos novos leilões que somam mais de 3.200 quilômetros e R$ 71,6 bilhões." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

*Operational implication:* the 2026 road-auction pipeline quoted above is a near-term signal for the workspace to monitor for new concessioned road corridors that could affect routing options or tolling on Brazilian lanes it uses.

FACT: "A expectativa é de geração de mais de 1,5 milhão de empregos, entre diretos, indiretos e efeito renda, além da melhoria da segurança viária, redução de custos logísticos e aumento da competitividade nacional." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

*Analytical inference:* the government's own stated expectation (over 1.5 million jobs, plus reduced logistics costs and increased national competitiveness) is a policy framing claim from the regulator itself, not an independently verified outcome; cited here as the government's own stated rationale for the investment programme, not as an established fact about logistics-cost reduction.

- 2023 to 2025: 19 road-concession auctions completed in Brazil (figures quoted in Section 7 above).
- 2026: new road auctions planned (figures quoted in Section 7 above); the government's rail-sector agenda for the year includes new auctions, contract renewals, and the Ferrogrão and EF-118 strategic projects.
- 15/04/2026: date of the ANTT news article this profile is grounded on.

*Note:* six captured blocks ground no claim in this brief, each returning site-navigation structure
rather than article or dataset content: the ANTT homepage (antt.gov.br), the ANTT portal landing page's
own navigation shell (gov.br/antt/pt-br, apart from the one news article above), the ANP (oil and gas
regulator) portal, the ANEEL (electricity regulator) portal (which additionally carries a
character-encoding defect in the small amount of body text it does contain, not reproduced as a quote
for that reason), the federal register access page (Diario Oficial da Uniao), and the Federal Senate
homepage.

# 1. Operational Cost Baseline for the Region

This profile synthesises current intelligence on operational costs, regulatory environment, infrastructure feasibility, and the road-freight decarbonisation landscape for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in India. It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is ocean, with air and road as secondary, operating across high-value and time-sensitive cargo verticals, with India serving Asia-Europe and Asia-Americas trade lanes plus significant domestic road-freight legs.

FACT: "Transport accounts for 14% of India’s GHG emissions, with medium and heavy-duty trucks responsible for 44% of that share—despite comprising just 3% of vehicles on the road." *Source: "India's Transport Transformation: Three Policies to Shape the Road Ahead," ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "India’s logistics costs, at about 13% of GDP, far exceed the global average." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "With 70% of freight moving by road and fuel making up a large portion of costs, electrifying trucks is both an environmental and economic imperative." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "Logistics costs remain high, with companies spending 10–15% of their expenses on transporting goods to and from factories." *Source: "Accelerating India's Freight Decarbonization," WRI India. https://wri-india.org/initiatives/accelerating-indias-freight-decarbonization

*Per the workspace's reading:* both sources independently confirm road freight's outsized cost and emissions footprint in India (70% of freight by road per ICCT; 10-15% of a shipping company's own expenses spent on transport per WRI India), which is the structural reason road-fleet decarbonisation and cost pressure are linked issues for a workspace's Indian road legs, not separate topics.

FACT: "The high upfront cost of electric trucks, coupled with limited charging infrastructure, remains a significant roadblock." *Source: WRI India. https://wri-india.org/initiatives/accelerating-indias-freight-decarbonization

**Industrial electricity and fuel pricing.**

GAP: Specific current diesel retail price (INR/litre, national average) is not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

GAP: Specific total-cost-of-ownership breakeven or payback period figures for electric versus diesel trucks in India are not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

FACT: "India has only 869 electric medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles." *Source: WRI India. https://wri-india.org/initiatives/accelerating-indias-freight-decarbonization

*Per the workspace's reading:* fewer than 900 electric medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles in service nationally is a very small base relative to India's overall truck fleet; electric road-freight capacity is not yet a scaled operational option for the workspace's Indian road legs.

FACT: "In July 2025, the Ministry of Heavy Industries released guidelines for electric trucks under the PM e-DRIVE scheme." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "By supporting electric trucks, e-DRIVE addresses three challenges at once: Reducing logistics costs through lower fuel dependency. Strengthening domestic manufacturing of advanced EV technologies such as heavy-duty batteries and charging systems. Improving air quality along highways and in cities, with health benefits for millions." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "BEE has released draft fuel-efficiency regulations for light-, medium-, and heavy-duty vehicles—regulations with immense potential to reshape the road transport sector." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "the Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines provide a framework to shrink the environmental footprint of ports—targeting over 60% renewable energy use by 2030 and 90% by 2047, electrifying half of port equipment by 2030 and 90% by 2047." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

*Analytical inference:* the Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines' own renewable-energy and port-equipment-electrification targets are staged out to 2030 and 2047; shore power and port electrification are policy-roadmap items, not yet operationally available at Indian ports at scale, per the captured pool.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Harit Sagar Guidelines are binding on port operators, or advisory only, is not established by the captured pool and requires legal confirmation before being cited to a client as a compliance requirement.

This omission will resolve once a second active region reaches sourced coverage on the same cost/feasibility dimensions.*

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: named-competitor sustainability positioning or certification data for freight operators in India is not available from the captured source blocks, which consist of an ICCT policy-analysis blog post and a WRI India initiative page rather than any operator's own published material.*

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- *Per the workspace's reading:* road transport is responsible for a disproportionate share of India's transport emissions (medium- and heavy-duty trucks are 44% of transport's GHG share while being only 3% of vehicles on the road) and a disproportionate share of cost (logistics run 10-15% of a shipping company's own expenses, and India's logistics costs overall are about 13% of GDP), which is why electrification and efficiency policy for trucks is a live, high-priority area of Indian government action.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* the PM e-DRIVE scheme (July 2025 guidelines) and Bureau of Energy Efficiency draft fuel-efficiency regulations are both active, named policy instruments the workspace can reference when discussing India's road-freight decarbonisation trajectory with a client.

**What the workspace should not claim without verification:**

- Do not present electric trucking as an operationally available choice for Indian road freight at any meaningful scale; fewer than 900 electric medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles are in service nationally per WRI India.
- *Legal Confirmation Required:* do not cite the Harit Sagar Guidelines as binding regulation on port operators; their enforcement status is not established by the captured pool.

**Questions the workspace can pose to clients:**

- "For your India-origin or India-destination shipments, is diesel fuel volatility or the 10-15%-of-expenses logistics cost burden the client's own team has flagged as the bigger near-term concern?"

*Analytical inference:* these talking points draw only on the FACT and GAP claims already established in Sections 1 and 2 above; no new fact is introduced in this section.

# 7. Pending Changes That Shift the Calculus

### MONITORING

FACT: "Raising industry awareness and securing commitments for 7,750 e-trucks at the Clean Energy Ministerial." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "It envisions expanding port capacity from 2,500 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA) today to more than 10,000 MMTPA, supported by world-class infrastructure, digital innovation, hydrogen and ammonia hubs, carbon-neutral operations, and shore power at all major ports by 2047." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

*Operational implication:* the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047's own port-capacity expansion target (2,500 to over 10,000 MMTPA) and its shore-power-at-all-major-ports-by-2047 goal are a multi-decade horizon; the workspace should track interim milestones rather than expect near-term port-side decarbonisation capacity.

GAP: A specific finalisation date for the BEE's draft heavy-duty-vehicle fuel-efficiency regulations is not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

- July 2025: Ministry of Heavy Industries released electric-truck guidelines under the PM e-DRIVE scheme.
- 2030: Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines target over 60% renewable energy use and half of port equipment electrified.
- 2047: Harit Sagar targets 90% renewable energy use and 90% port-equipment electrification; Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 targets over 10,000 MMTPA port capacity and shore power at all major ports.

# 1. Operational Cost Baseline for the Region

This profile synthesises current intelligence on operational costs, infrastructure investment, and the road/rail freight regulatory environment for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in Brazil. It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is ocean, with road and air as secondary/tertiary, operating across high-value and time-sensitive cargo verticals, with Brazilian gateways serving South American and transatlantic trade lanes and significant domestic road-freight legs.

FACT: "Salvar vidas e ainda proteger a carga que representa cerca de 50% do PIB do país!" *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation portal. https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br

*Per the workspace's reading:* the Ministry's own framing puts road-carried cargo at roughly 50% of Brazil's GDP, underscoring why national road-investment programmes (below) are directly material to the cost and reliability of the workspace's Brazilian road legs.

FACT: "Com investimento de R$ 407,8 milhões, duplicação da BR-080 avança entre Taguatinga e Brazlândia Durante visita técnica, ministro dos Transportes George Santoro acompanhou o andamento das intervenções, que já alcançam cerca de 20% de execução" *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation portal. https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br

FACT: "Ministério dos Transportes destina R$ 1,45 bilhão para melhorias no Trecho do Meio da BR-319/AM Recursos contemplam intervenções em 339 quilômetros da rodovia, divididos em quatro lotes" *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation portal. https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br

FACT: "Consórcio 116 Sertões vence certame da BR-116/324/BA/PE com aporte de R$ 8,53 bilhões em infraestrutura" *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation portal. https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br

FACT: "Transporte Rodoviário de Cargas - TRC" *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation portal. https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br

*Per the workspace's reading:* "Transporte Rodoviário de Cargas" (Road Freight Transport, TRC) is the Ministry's own named regulatory category for road freight; it is the active regulatory framework the workspace's Brazilian road-freight subcontractors operate under, though the captured pool does not detail its specific compliance requirements (Section 5).

**Industrial electricity and fuel pricing.**

GAP: Specific current industrial electricity rates, diesel fuel retail prices, drayage costs, and port handling tariffs are not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

FACT: "Compared with diesel-powered vehicles, electric vehicles deliver approximately 80% lower operating costs, 80% to over 100% higher energy efficiency, greater comfort for passengers and drivers, and the elimination of particulate matter, polluting gases, and CO2." *Source: Global Drive to Zero, "Charging Up Change: Brazil Accelerating its Drive to Zero." https://globaldrivetozero.org/2025/11/03/charging-up-change-brazil-accelerating-its-drive-to-zero/

FACT: "Brazil saw a 141 percent increase in new zero-emission bus sales in the first half of 2025." *Source: Global Drive to Zero. https://globaldrivetozero.org/2025/11/03/charging-up-change-brazil-accelerating-its-drive-to-zero/

FACT: "more than 1,380 commercial electric vehicles were sold in the country between January and July 2025, including vans, buses, and trucks according to the ABVE." *Source: Global Drive to Zero. https://globaldrivetozero.org/2025/11/03/charging-up-change-brazil-accelerating-its-drive-to-zero/

FACT: "EZVolt, the largest electromobility company in Brazil, services roughly 75% of the e-bus fleets from São Paulo city." *Source: Global Drive to Zero. https://globaldrivetozero.org/2025/11/03/charging-up-change-brazil-accelerating-its-drive-to-zero/

FACT: "The city has banned the purchase of new diesel buses, and is aiming to have a 100% zero-emission fleet by 2038, along with significant reductions in particulate matter and other pollutants." *Source: Global Drive to Zero (reporting on São Paulo city policy). https://globaldrivetozero.org/2025/11/03/charging-up-change-brazil-accelerating-its-drive-to-zero/

*Analytical inference:* the evidence base for electrified fleets in Brazil is currently concentrated in the urban bus segment (São Paulo's 100% zero-emission target by 2038, EZVolt servicing roughly 75% of São Paulo's e-bus fleet); the captured pool gives no equivalent adoption evidence for heavy-duty freight trucking specifically (Section 5).

FACT: "Brazil launched the MOVER program (Programa Nacional de Mobilidade Verde e Inovação), which is the first of its kind to regulate emissions from the heavy-duty transportation sector (with specific regulations expected for 2027/8)." *Source: Global Drive to Zero. https://globaldrivetozero.org/2025/11/03/charging-up-change-brazil-accelerating-its-drive-to-zero/

FACT: "Brazil has around 10,000 kilometers of idle railway lines. The proposal is to reactivate these sections through new concession models with contracts of up to 99 years and free tariffs." *Source: U.S. International Trade Administration, "Brazil Rail Transportation." https://www.trade.gov/market-intelligence/brazil-rail-transportation

FACT: "The first section to be offered is the Minas-Rio railway corridor (Central-Atlantic Railway). The selection process will begin between September and October 2025." *Source: U.S. ITA. https://www.trade.gov/market-intelligence/brazil-rail-transportation

FACT: "This model allows for the introduction of advanced U.S. freight rail technologies, including alternative energy sources, digital solutions, and specialized equipment, to meet the growing demand for modern railway infrastructure." *Source: U.S. ITA. https://www.trade.gov/market-intelligence/brazil-rail-transportation

*Operational implication:* the reactivation of roughly 10,000 kilometers of idle Brazilian railway line via a new long-term (up to 99-year) concession model, starting with the Minas-Rio corridor, is a real modal-diversification signal for a workspace with Brazilian inland freight; the workspace should monitor the Minas-Rio selection process outcome (Section 7) as the first test of this model.

# 3. Cost Comparison Against Alternatives

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: specific numerical breakeven or payback data comparing operational choices (rail vs road, electric vs diesel fleet total cost of ownership specific to freight trucking) in the Brazilian context are not available from the sourced blocks beyond the general EV-vs-diesel operating-cost and efficiency figures already quoted in Section 2. This section is replaced by this honest note rather than filled with invented figures.*

# 4. Cross-Regional Strategic Implications

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: Cross-Regional Strategic Implications is a MATRIX-then-transitive comparison requiring the same cost or feasibility dimension sourced across at least two of the workspace's active regions. This record's stored pool covers only Brazil; no other regional_data item's sourced figures were supplied for this authoring pass, so no cross-regional comparison can be proven from this single stored pool. This omission will resolve once a second active region reaches sourced coverage on the same cost/feasibility dimensions.*

# 5. Competitive Positioning in the Region

FACT: "The platform connects innovators and stakeholders from across the freight and logistics value chain, including industry, financial institutions, and government." *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation portal (e-FAST Brasil platform). https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br

*Analytical inference:* e-FAST Brasil is a government-run platform explicitly for connecting freight-and-logistics-value-chain stakeholders (industry, financial institutions, government); a workspace active in Brazilian freight could evaluate participation as a visibility channel for government-adjacent freight-sustainability initiatives, though the captured pool does not detail participation requirements or cost.

GAP: Zero-emission heavy truck availability in Brazil remains limited to early-stage models and pilot-scale fleets per the captured pool; no named competitor's heavy-duty freight electrification programme is identified.

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- *Per the workspace's reading:* the Brazilian Ministry of Transportation's own framing states that road-carried cargo represents roughly 50% of the country's GDP, underscoring why the government's road-investment programme (including the BR-080, BR-319, and BR-116/324 projects quoted above) is directly relevant to Brazilian road-freight reliability and cost.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* Brazil's electric-vehicle sustainability programme (MOVER) is the first of its kind to regulate heavy-duty transport emissions, with specific regulations expected in 2027/8; this is a concrete, dated compliance horizon to flag to clients planning Brazilian fleet or subcontractor decisions.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* a new long-term rail concession model targeting roughly 10,000 kilometers of currently idle Brazilian railway, starting with the Minas-Rio corridor, is a real (if early-stage) rail modal-diversification option to watch for Brazilian inland freight.

**What the workspace should not claim without verification:**

- Do not present electrified heavy-duty freight trucking as an operationally available choice in Brazil today; the evidence base in the captured pool is concentrated in urban buses, not freight trucks.
- Do not cite a specific Brazilian industrial electricity tariff, diesel price, drayage cost, or port handling tariff; none is available from the captured pool.

**Questions the workspace can pose to clients:**

- "For your Brazilian inland freight, would a long-term rail concession corridor like Minas-Rio be a routing option worth evaluating once it reaches operational status, or is road the only viable mode for your current lanes?"

*Analytical inference:* these talking points draw only on the FACT and GAP claims already established in Sections 1, 2, and 5 above; no new fact is introduced in this section.

# 7. Pending Changes That Shift the Calculus

### MONITORING

FACT: "Concessões Rodoviárias 2026" *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation portal. https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br

FACT: "Primeiro leilão rodoviário no Nordeste tem maior desconto na tarifa por quilômetro Consórcio 116 Sertões vence certame da BR-116/324/BA/PE com aporte de R$ 8,53 bilhões em infraestrutura" *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation portal. https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br

FACT: "Trecho que liga Feira de Santana (BA) a Salgueiro (PE) é considerado estratégico para o abastecimento regional, o transporte de cargas e a mobilidade da população" *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation portal. https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br

FACT: "integração de critérios de sustentabilidade, gestão de riscos, adaptação à mudança do clima e classificação das atividades econômicas segundo a Taxonomia Sustentável Brasileira, especialmente no que se refere às atividades enquadradas na CNAE H – Transporte, Armazenagem e Correio." *Source: Brazilian Ministry of Transportation, Sustainability page. https://www.gov.br/transportes/pt-br/assuntos/sustentabilidade

*Operational implication:* the Ministry's own Sustainability sub-secretariat explicitly names CNAE H (Transport, Storage and Mail) as a sector the Brazilian Sustainable Taxonomy classification framework applies to; a workspace or client operating a Brazilian-registered transport entity should monitor whether taxonomy classification becomes a disclosure or financing precondition.

- September-October 2025: selection process begins for the Minas-Rio railway corridor, the first section offered under Brazil's new long-term rail concession model.
- 2027/8: MOVER programme's specific heavy-duty-transport emissions regulations expected.
- 2038: São Paulo city's target for a 100% zero-emission bus fleet.

This item's title names IEA electricity price data for large industrial customers (2019-2024); every one of the six IEA captures in this item's stored pool, and the European Commission's finance-portal homepage, returned only a Cloudflare security-verification interstitial or a bare language-selection page (Section 8), so none of them grounds any claim below. The one real-content capture in this pool is Eurostat's own Electricity Price Statistics article, which is EU-wide (not IEA-sourced) and reports household and non-household (not specifically large-industrial) price bands. This profile is authored as an EU electricity-cost baseline on that basis; the specific IEA large-industrial-customer comparison the title names is a genuine GAP (Section 5), not silently substituted.

FACT: "electricity prices in the second half of 2025 were highest in Ireland (€0.2552 per kWh), Cyprus (€0.2429 per kWh) and Germany(€0.2264 per kWh). The lowest prices were observed in Finland (€0.0748 per kWh) and Sweden (€0.0970 per kWh). The EU average price in the second half of 2025 was €0.1837 per kWh." *Source: Electricity Price Statistics, Eurostat (European Commission). https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

*Per the workspace's reading:* non-household electricity prices (the closest band in this pool to a commercial/logistics-facility rate, though not specifically the large-industrial-customer band the item title names) show an over 3x spread across EU member states in H2 2025 (figures quoted above, Finland lowest and Ireland highest) -- a workspace with facilities or subcontractors in multiple EU countries should expect materially different electricity cost exposure by country, not a single EU-wide rate.

entries.body:
# 1. Operational Cost Baseline for the Region

This profile synthesises current intelligence on energy costs, market conditions, and the road-freight electrification trend for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in the EU. It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is ocean, with air and road as secondary, operating across high-value and time-sensitive cargo verticals, with EU core-market gateways serving intra-European and transatlantic/Asia trade lanes.

FACT: "The EU quarterly gas and electricity market reports analyse market data in detail to examine trends and challenges." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, Market Analysis quarterly reports. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "The 6th report on energy prices and costs  was published in February 2025." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, Energy Prices and Costs in Europe. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "although the EU’s energy import bill receded to €427 billion in 2024 (after reaching the peak of €604 billion in 2022), is still a significant drain on the European economy." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, Energy Prices and Costs in Europe (6th report). https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "industrial gas and electricity prices, while lower than during the crisis, are still 2-4 times higher than in the EU’s main trading partners, which threatens the long-term competitiveness of European industry." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, Energy Prices and Costs in Europe. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

*Operational implication:* the Commission's own finding that EU industrial gas and electricity prices remain 2-4x higher than in the EU's main trading partners is a direct, structural cost disadvantage for any EU-based logistics or warehousing facility relative to non-EU competitors; this is the single most material cost-baseline fact in this profile for a workspace evaluating EU facility investment.

FACT: "due notably to the time lag in transmission of prices between the two market segments, the drop in wholesale prices is yet to bring down retail energy prices , which are still higher for households and enterprises than before 2021." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "Household gas prices were almost twice as high in 2023 than before the crisis." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "Wholesale prices have stabilised on both electricity and gas markets since the energy crisis of 2021-2023, although at a level higher than their historical averages." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "European wholesale prices averaged 35 €/MWh in the second quarter of 2025, a significant decrease of 24% compared to the previous quarter and a 10% increase year-on-year." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU gas market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Retail gas prices decreased by 2% compared to the previous quarter and increased by 9% year-on-year. The EU quarterly average retail price was 110 €/MWh." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU gas market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Retail electricity prices for households in EU capital cities rose marginally by 3% in Q2 2025 (to 246 €/MWh)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU electricity market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Additionally, there was significant variation between EU countries with several seeing double-digit percentage increases (e.g. Austria, Luxembourg, Poland) and others seeing large decreases in retail prices due to lower energy costs (e.g. Slovenia, Estonia, France)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

*Per the workspace's reading:* EU retail electricity prices are not uniform across member states (Austria, Luxembourg and Poland saw double-digit increases in Q2 2025 while Slovenia, Estonia and France saw large decreases); a workspace evaluating EU facility siting should treat this as country-level variation, not a single "EU electricity price."

GAP: Country-level commercial/industrial electricity rates by EU Member State are not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

FACT: "Finally, with over 720 000 new electric vehicles sold in Q2 2025, the quarter set an all-time record for sales of EVs in the passenger car segment in the EU - a yearly increase of almost 30% compared with Q2 2024." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU electricity market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "This translates into a 23% EV share in the EU passenger car market, more than two times the market share registered in the United States (10%)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

*Analytical inference:* an EU passenger-car EV share more than double the US share (23% versus 10%) is not a direct read on freight-vehicle electrification, but it does indicate the charging-infrastructure and public-policy environment supporting electrification is materially more advanced in EU core markets than in some other regions -- context relevant when a client asks why the workspace treats EU road-fleet electrification differently from other regions.

FACT: "The electricity market report   Q2 2025   confirms that solar generation rose to a new record high for a second quarter, reaching 98 TWh (+20%)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU electricity market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "The share of renewables stayed stable at 52% in Q2 2025 (same as in Q2 2024), while the share of fossil fuels rose very slightly to 25% (from 24% in Q2 2024)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Electricity consumption in the EU stayed flat (+0.4%) compared with Q2 2024." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

GAP: Specific feasibility data, permitting requirements, or grid connection lead times for on-site solar and battery energy storage systems (BESS) at EU logistics facilities are not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

# 3. Cost Comparison Against Alternatives

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: specific numerical breakeven or payback data for on-site solar vs grid power, or EV vs diesel road-fleet total cost of ownership specific to freight trucking, in the EU context are not available from the sourced blocks. This section is replaced by this honest note rather than filled with invented figures.*

# 4. Cross-Regional Strategic Implications

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: Cross-Regional Strategic Implications is a MATRIX-then-transitive comparison requiring the same cost or feasibility dimension sourced across at least two of the workspace's active regions. This record's stored pool covers only the EU; no other regional_data item's sourced figures were supplied for this authoring pass, so no cross-regional comparison can be proven from this single stored pool, even though the Commission's own 2-4x industrial-price finding above (Section 1) names EXACTLY the kind of cross-regional comparison this section would make once a second region's sourced figures are available. This omission will resolve once a second active region reaches sourced coverage on the same cost dimension.*

# 5. Competitive Positioning in the Region

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: named-competitor sustainability or energy-sourcing positioning data for freight operators in the EU is not available from the captured source blocks, which consist of European Commission market-analysis pages rather than any operator's own published material.*

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- *Per the workspace's reading:* the European Commission's own analysis finds EU industrial gas and electricity prices are still 2-4 times higher than in the EU's main trading partners, a structural competitiveness factor for any EU-based logistics operation, not a temporary condition.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* the EU's energy import bill eased from its 2022 peak by 2024 (figures quoted in Section 1), but the Commission itself still calls it "a significant drain on the European economy" -- useful context for why EU energy-cost pressure, while easing, has not resolved.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* EV sales in the EU passenger-car segment hit an all-time quarterly record in Q2 2025 (over 720,000 vehicles, 23% market share), more than double the US market share, evidence the EU's charging and policy environment for electrification is comparatively mature.

**What the workspace should not claim without verification:**

- Do not present a single "EU electricity price"; retail electricity price movement varies materially by member state (Section 1).
- Do not extrapolate the EU's strong passenger-car EV adoption to heavy-duty freight trucking; the captured pool's EV figures are for the passenger-car segment specifically.

*Analytical inference:* these talking points draw only on the FACT and GAP claims already established in Sections 1 and 2 above; no new fact is introduced in this section.

# 7. Pending Changes That Shift the Calculus

### MONITORING

GAP: The ETS2 emissions trading scheme is scheduled to extend to cover road transport fuel in a future compliance phase, adding a carbon-cost layer to diesel and LNG road-freight fuel; the specific per-tonne carbon cost for road freight is not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

FACT: "The share of LNG in overall EU gas supply further increased to 46%. Pipeline gas supply from Russia halved year-on-year and decreased by 15% compared to the previous quarter." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU gas market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "The U.S. has become the second largest EU gas supplier with 27%, next to Norway, which kept its number one position by 30%." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Russia’s share in overall EU gas supplied declined to 12% by 6 percentage points year-on-year." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU gas market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

*Operational implication:* the continued structural shift of EU gas supply away from Russia (down to a 12% share) and toward LNG (46% of supply, led by the US) is the underlying driver of the price volatility and elevated levels described in Section 1; the workspace should track this diversification trend as the leading indicator for future EU energy-cost direction, not treat current prices as a stable baseline.

- February 2025: the European Commission published its 6th report on Energy Prices and Costs in Europe.
- Q2 2025: the reporting quarter for the gas and electricity market data quoted throughout this profile.

This profile synthesises current intelligence on air-quality permitting, dust-control requirements, and the regulatory environment for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in Clark County, Nevada (Las Vegas metro area). It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is air, with road as secondary, operating across high-value and time-sensitive cargo verticals, with Clark County serving as a US gateway and warehousing/distribution hub.

FACT: "The Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability, Division of Air Quality (DAQ) administers the air pollution control program for Clark County, Nevada under provisions of the Clark County Air Quality Regulations (AQRs)." *Source: Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability, Division of Air Quality. https://clarkcountynv.gov/government/departments/environment_and_sustainability/index.php

FACT: "DAQ issues major and minor stationary source permits (AQRs 12.0-12.5 and 12.11) as well as dust control operating permits (AQR 94)." *Source: Clark County DAQ, Current AQ Rules index. https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/departments/environment_and_sustainability/division_of_air_quality/rules___regulations/current-aq-rules

FACT: "Section 18 – Permit and Technical Service Fees –Effective 2/12/2026" *Source: Clark County DAQ, Current AQ Rules index. https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/departments/environment_and_sustainability/division_of_air_quality/rules___regulations/current-aq-rules

*Per the workspace's reading:* the permit and technical service fee schedule (Section 18) was itself updated effective 2/12/2026; a workspace or client operating a permitted Clark County facility should confirm current fee amounts against this schedule rather than a prior-year figure.

**Industrial electricity, fuel, and labor cost baseline.**

GAP: No sourced, dated cost figure (industrial electricity, fuel, labor, port handling, or drayage) for Clark County, Nevada is present in the captured source blocks.

FACT: "The Clark County Small Business Assistance Program provides no-cost permitting and compliance assistance for facilities in Clark County. If you’re a small business (100 or fewer employees) and not a major stationary source for air pollutants, you qualify for their services." *Source: University of Nevada, Reno Business Environmental Program (Clark County air-quality assistance page). https://unrbep.org/services/air-quality-assistance-homepage/clark-county-air-assistance/

*Analytical inference:* the Small Business Assistance Program's no-cost permitting help is scoped to facilities of 100 or fewer employees that are not major stationary sources; it is relevant context for a small Clark County subcontractor or warehouse partner, but the workspace's own larger operations, or a major-source client facility, would not qualify.

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

FACT: "Section 45 – Idling of Diesel Powered Motor Vehicles –Amended 8/3/2021 (Ordinance 4878)" *Source: Clark County DAQ, Current AQ Rules index. https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/departments/environment_and_sustainability/division_of_air_quality/rules___regulations/current-aq-rules

*Operational implication:* Clark County's diesel-idling rule (AQR Section 45) directly constrains road-fleet and yard-vehicle operations at any Clark County facility or subcontractor; a workspace should confirm its own or its subcontractors' idling practices are compliant, particularly at loading docks and staging areas.

FACT: "Section 94 – Permitting and Dust Control for Construction and Temporary Commercial Activities –Amended 12/17/2024 –Effective 1/1/2025 (Ordinance 5205 )" *Source: Clark County DAQ, Current AQ Rules index. https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/departments/environment_and_sustainability/division_of_air_quality/rules___regulations/current-aq-rules

FACT: "Section 92 – Fugitive Dust Control Requirements for Unpaved Parking Lots and Storage Areas –Amended 12/17/2024 –Effective 1/1/2025 (Ordinance 5205 )" *Source: Clark County DAQ, Current AQ Rules index. https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/departments/environment_and_sustainability/division_of_air_quality/rules___regulations/current-aq-rules

FACT: "A Dust Control Operating Permit is required for soil disturbing or construction activities 0.25 acres or greater in overall area, mechanized trenching one hundred (100) feet or greater in length, or for mechanical demolition of any structure one thousand (1,000) square feet or larger, or for Temporary Commercial Activities 0.25 acres or greater in overall area." *Source: Clark County DAQ, Dust Permitting Forms. https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/departments/environment_and_sustainability/division_of_air_quality/permitting/applications_forms/dust-permitting-forms

FACT: "The thresholds for requiring a dust control operating permit for construction or temporary commercial activities can be found in AQR 94.4.1(b)." *Source: Clark County DAQ, Dust Permitting Forms. https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/departments/environment_and_sustainability/division_of_air_quality/permitting/applications_forms/dust-permitting-forms

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- *Per the workspace's reading:* Clark County operates its own air-quality regulatory programme (the Division of Air Quality, administering the Clark County Air Quality Regulations) with specific, dated rules on diesel-vehicle idling (Section 45), stationary-source permitting (Section 12 series), and construction/dust control (Sections 92 and 94) -- a workspace can confirm its own or a subcontractor's Clark County compliance status against these named, current sections.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* dust-control permitting thresholds are specific and checkable (0.25 acres of soil disturbance, 100 feet of trenching, or 1,000 square feet of demolition), directly relevant to any Clark County facility expansion or ground-disturbing project the workspace or a client is planning.

**What the workspace should not claim without verification:**

- Do not cite a specific Clark County industrial electricity, fuel, labor, port-handling, or drayage cost figure; none is available from the captured pool.
- Do not assume the Small Business Assistance Program's no-cost compliance help applies to a major stationary source or a facility with more than 100 employees; the programme is explicitly scoped to smaller, non-major-source facilities.

**Questions the workspace can pose to clients:**

- "Does your Clark County facility's ground-disturbing footprint (construction, trenching, or demolition) exceed the county's 0.25-acre/100-foot/1,000-square-foot dust-permit thresholds, and if so, has a Dust Control Operating Permit been obtained?"

*Analytical inference:* these talking points draw only on the FACT and GAP claims already established in Sections 1 and 2 above; no new fact is introduced in this section.

*Operational implication:* the Section 12.2-12.5 stationary-source permit requirements were all amended by Ordinance 5375 (effective 6/3/2026), and Section 12.5 (Part 70 Operating Permit Requirements) is explicitly noted as "under EPA review" -- a workspace or client with a major-source Clark County facility should track the outcome of that EPA review, since it could change Part 70 operating-permit requirements again.
